pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B7.3.1)
- B7.3.1.2 — Demonstrate how to construct a perpendicular to a line from a given point, bisect a line, bisect angles, and construct angles of the following sizes: 30°, 45°, 60°, 75° and 90°.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- copy a line segment with a pair of compasses and a ruler
- construct a perpendicular at a point on a line and from a point outside a line
- construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment
- copy and bisect angles
- construct angles of 90°, 45°, 60°, 30°, 15° and 75°
- recognise perpendiculars and bisectors in the environment

pages.title: Copying a line segment and constructing perpendiculars
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Construct a line segment perpendicular to another line segment.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.2.1
## ✏️ Example 9.1
Construct RS, a copy of the line segment PQ.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f39]]
Figure 9.1: Copying line segment PQ
1. Draw a straight line and mark a point R on it.
2. Open the compasses to the length PQ (point on P, pencil on Q).
3. Without changing the width, put the point on R and draw an arc to cut the line at S.
4. RS = PQ.
## ✏️ Example 9.2
Construct a perpendicular to line AB at the point P on it.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f40]]
Figure 9.2: Perpendicular at a point P on a line
1. With centre P and any radius, draw arcs to cut the line at X and Y (PX = PY).
2. With centres X and Y and a larger radius, draw arcs that cross above the line at Q.
3. Join PQ. PQ is perpendicular to AB (∠QPB = 90°).
## ✏️ Example 9.3
Drop a perpendicular from a point P outside the line AB.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f41]]
Figure 9.3: Perpendicular from an external point P
1. With centre P, draw an arc to cut AB at X and Y.
2. With centres X and Y and the same radius, draw arcs that cross on the other side of AB at Q.
3. Join PQ, cutting AB at N. PN is the perpendicular from P to AB, and PN is the **shortest distance** from P to the line.
> ✏️ **Practice:** Exercise 9.1, at the end of section 9.2, covers this section too. Tap **Quick check** to try its questions.

questions.q: Draw a triangle of any shape. Construct the perpendicular bisector of each side. What do you notice?

parts.a: The three perpendicular bisectors meet at one point.

pages.title: The perpendicular bisector of a line segment
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.2.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Perpendicular bisector** — A **perpendicular bisector** of a line segment cuts it into two equal parts **and** is at right angles to it. Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is the same distance from A as from B.
## ✏️ Example 9.4
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB = 8 cm.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f42]]
Figure 9.4: CD is the perpendicular bisector of AB
1. Draw AB = 8 cm.
2. With centre A and radius more than half of AB (say 5 cm), draw arcs above and below AB.
3. With centre B and the same radius, draw arcs to cut the first arcs at C and D.
4. Join CD, cutting AB at M. Then AM = MB = 4 cm and CD ⊥ AB.

pages.title: Exercise 9.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 9.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Draw a line segment AB = 7.4 cm and construct a copy of it.
2. Draw a line and mark a point P on it. Construct a perpendicular at P.
3. Mark a point P 4 cm above a line. Construct the perpendicular from P to the line and measure its length.
4. Draw and bisect: a) AB = 8 cm b) AB = 5.5 cm. Measure each half.
5. Draw a triangle of any shape. Construct the perpendicular bisector of each side. What do you notice?

questions.q: Draw a triangle of any shape. Construct the perpendicular bisector of each side. What do you notice?

parts.a: The three perpendicular bisectors meet at one point.

pages.title: Copying and bisecting angles
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Copy and bisect angles.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.2.3
## ✏️ Example 9.5
Copy a given angle A.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f43]]
Figure 9.5: Copying ∠A to make ∠B
1. Draw a line and mark a point B on it.
2. With centre A and any radius, draw an arc cutting the arms of ∠A at S and T.
3. With centre B and the same radius, draw an arc cutting the line at V.
4. Set the compasses to the distance ST. With centre V draw an arc cutting the first arc at W.
5. Join B to W. ∠WBV = ∠A.
## ✏️ Example 9.6
Bisect a given angle ∠BAC.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f44]]
Figure 9.6: AD bisects ∠BAC
1. With centre A, draw an arc cutting AB at P and AC at Q.
2. With centres P and Q and the same radius, draw arcs that cross at D.
3. Join AD. AD is the **angle bisector**: ∠BAD = ∠DAC.
> 🧪 **Activity 9.1 — Checking with a partner**
(i) Sketch any acute angle and label it ABC. (ii) Copy the angle by construction, measure both angles and record their values. (iii) Sketch any angle and ask a classmate to copy and bisect it. Check each other's work with a protractor.
## ✏️ Example 9.7
Which of these figures shows a correct angle bisector? Explain.
[[fig:m7-f45]]
Figure 9.7: Which is a correct angle bisector?
**Solution**
Measure the two parts of each angle. Only in **figure b)** are the two parts equal (35° and 35°), so it is the only correct bisector. In a) the parts are 30° and 50°; in c) the line is not drawn from the vertex.

pages.title: Constructing angles of 90° and 45°
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Construct angles of 90° and 45°.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.2.4
## ✏️ Example 9.8
Construct ∠APB = 90° at a point P on a line and verify with a protractor.
**Solution**
Raise a perpendicular at P (Example 9.2). The angle between the perpendicular and the line is 90°. Check with a protractor.
## ✏️ Example 9.9
Construct ∠ABC = 45° such that AB = 5 cm and BC = 6 cm.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f46]]
Figure 9.8: Bisecting a right angle gives 45°
1. Draw BC = 6 cm. At B construct a perpendicular BD (∠DBC = 90°).
2. Bisect ∠DBC. The bisector makes an angle of 45° with BC.
3. Mark A on the bisector so that BA = 5 cm. ∠ABC = 45°.
> ✏️ **Practice:** Exercise 9.2, at the end of section 9.6, covers this section too. Tap **Quick check** to try its questions.

pages.title: Constructing angles of 60° and 30°
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Construct angles of 60° and 30°.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.2.5
## ✏️ Example 9.10
Construct ∠ABC = 60° at a point B on a line and verify with a protractor.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f47]]
Figure 9.9: Constructing 60°
1. Draw a line BC. With centre B and any radius, draw a large arc cutting BC at P.
2. With centre P and the **same radius**, draw an arc cutting the first arc at Q.
3. Join B to Q and extend to A. ∠ABC = 60°.
(B, P and Q form an equilateral triangle, so each of its angles is 60°.)
## ✏️ Example 9.11
Construct an angle of 30°.
**Solution**
Construct ∠AOB = 60° and then bisect it. The bisector OC gives ∠AOC = ∠COB = **30°**.
> ✏️ **Practice:** Exercise 9.2, at the end of section 9.6, covers this section too. Tap **Quick check** to try its questions.

pages.title: Constructing angles of 15° and 75°
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Construct angles whose measures are 15° and 75°.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.2.6
## ✏️ Example 9.12
Construct an angle of 15°.
**Solution**
Construct 60°, bisect it to get 30°, then bisect the 30° angle. Each part is **15°**.
## ✏️ Example 9.13
Construct an angle of 75° at a point O on a line.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f48]]
Figure 9.10: 75° = 60° + 15°, the bisector of the angle between 60° and 90°
1. At O construct ∠AOB = 90° (perpendicular OB).
2. On the same arc, construct ∠AOM = 60° (point M on the arc).
3. Bisect the arc MN between the 60° line and the 90° line (i.e. bisect ∠MOB = 30°) to get point P.
4. Join O through P. ∠AOP = 60° + 15° = **75°**.

pages.title: Exercise 9.2
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 9.2** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Construct each angle and check with a protractor: a) ∠PQR = 75° b) ∠ABC = 60° c) ∠KLM = 30° d) ∠RST = 15° e) ∠XYZ = 90° f) 45°
2. Construct ∠PQR = 75° and then bisect it. What is the size of each part?
3. Construct ∠ABC = 90° and bisect it. Then bisect one of the 45° angles. What angle do you get?
4. Construct triangle ABC with BC = 7 cm, ∠ABC = 60° and ∠ACB = 45°. Measure AB and ∠BAC.
5. Explain how you would construct an angle of 120° (Hint: 180° − 60°).

pages.title: Perpendiculars and bisectors in our environment
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Describe examples of perpendicular line segments, perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors in the environment.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.2.7
Look around you. Builders, carpenters, tailors and engineers use perpendiculars and bisectors every day:
The corners of doors, windows, tables, books and blackboards are **perpendicular** edges (90°).
The vertical support in the middle of a roof truss is the **perpendicular bisector** of the beam it stands on.
The ridge of a symmetrical roof, the central fold of a kente strip pattern, or the line of symmetry of an Adinkra symbol often **bisects an angle**.
The legs of a cylindrical water tank stand perpendicular to the ground.
[[fig:m7-f49|Figure 9.11: A roof truss: the king post is the perpendicular bisector of the tie beam and bisects the apex angle]]
> 🧪 **Activity 9.2 — Angles around us**
Work in groups. Walk around the school compound and list at least five examples each of perpendicular lines, perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors (buildings, water tanks, boxes, goal posts, furniture). Estimate the size of angles in artefacts and tools (e.g. a pair of scissors opened, the roof of the classroom, a hoe handle and blade), then measure them where possible. Present your findings with sketches.

pages.title: Chapter 9 summary
pages.body:
- Use only a ruler and a pair of compasses to construct; use a protractor only to check.
- Perpendicular bisector: equal arcs from both ends of the segment.
- Angle bisector: equal arcs from the arms of the angle.
- 60°: equilateral-triangle arcs; 30° = half of 60°; 15° = half of 30°; 90°: perpendicular; 45° = half of 90°; 75° = 60° + 15°.

Draw any obtuse angle and bisect it. Measure each part.

parts.a: Each part is half of the angle
